extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; aspiring writers and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative principles and practical guidance for judging writers and for authorship — covering originality, style, motives for writing, quantity vs quality, balance of life and work, and ethical modes of criticism. Drawn from 19th-century literary-critical prose and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge by quantity of grain not of chaff
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us judge the 'worthy Teutones' as thinkers and writers, not by the quantity of their chaff, but by the quantity of their grain; the good grain which already enters into our own loaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract and reward the solid matter in a body of work rather than condemning the whole for surrounding 'unsound' material. Be prepared to 'abstract the solid matter from the mass of the unsound that floats around it' and to credit worthwhile ideas even when embedded in a larger, less valuable context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value exploratory, free spirit of enterprise in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: They write far more ... in a free spirit of enterprise, that takes no bond beforehand, but carries on the adventurer with hopes the larger because undefined, and very slight fears of censure or contempt. They go exploring in all directions ... acting in this spirit, they have made discoveries in fruitful regions, while the English have been making none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage adventurous, wide-ranging literary exploration despite many fruitless attempts; contrast this with the conservative 'pompous measured gait' of following beaten tracks. Anti-pattern: excessive deference to tradition that prevents discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize trade-off: more thinking/new ideas can reduce stylistic smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: Germans ... think more, and have a greater number of new thoughts to provide with new apparel. The streams of language run less smoothly when they are flowing through freshly-opened channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that originality and dense thinking may result in less polished or less 'smooth' prose; evaluate works with sensitivity to this trade-off between novelty of thought and fluency of expression rather than penalizing awkwardness that arises from genuine innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pursue literature as the sole business of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Never pursue Literature as the sole business of life or the means on which you rely for obtaining its comforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical counsel to writers: making literature one's only livelihood risks starving the writer or debasing literature itself. Professional authorship can force quantity-driven, low-quality output. Example/claim: Had some celebrated authors not needed to sell so much, their work might have been fewer but weightier and better structured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write from nature or persuasion, not as a trade
rubrics_metrics.description: If nature prompts you, or if friends persuade. Why write, but ne'er pursue it as a trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation for writing should be intrinsic (nature) or sincere encouragement, not commercial pressure. Anti-patterns include writing 'gay conundrums ... or earn by defamation daily bread'—i.e., pandering to the market or producing scandal for pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer fewer, more perfect works over voluminous output
rubrics_metrics.description: their productions might have been less in quantity, weightier, as to the whole mass, in quality; and I believe ... fewer volumes of romance but more perfect romances, compositions more careful in structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality, structural care, and perfection of composition trump high volume of production. Producing many works for immediate sale often sacrifices depth and careful structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid letting intellectual pursuits override domestic affections
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not permit the interests of an intellectual pursuit thus to over-ride those of the affections; the two should be made to bear equally upon the moral being and to subserve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical/ethical guidance for writers: balance literary/intellectual work with family and personal responsibilities. Anti-pattern: treating philosophy or literature as a substitute for domestic commitment, thereby harming relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique works not personal character
rubrics_metrics.description: Would that all who enter into such contests confined themselves ... to describing the literary offences themselves, instead of descanting on the affairs, motives, feelings, and personal character of those that have committed them!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical norm for criticism: address literary faults and merits, avoid ad hominem attacks, and limit commentary to works rather than private lives or motives of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be obsessed with immediate fame; time settles judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Old Time will settle all your claims at once, Record the genius and forget the dunce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term reputation and lasting value are the proper measures; instantaneous lists, rankings or popular applause are unreliable measures of lasting merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for individuality; avoid mere imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: This Ode ... has everytHing that is to be desired, except a soul of its own; it reads like a first-rate school exercise ... poems produced by Talent apart from Genius ... have scarce any individualizing characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek a distinctive voice and 'soul' in composition; beware of technically accomplished but derivative writing that lacks originality and individualizing characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance ambitious scope with capacity to execute
rubrics_metrics.description: He was 'many-sided' ... the same all-grasping ambition ... title-pages alone (titles of works meditated but unexecuted) would fill a large volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition and breadth must be matched by the ability to complete and execute projects; excessive proliferation of planned works can indicate overreach and lead to superficiality or an accumulation of unfulfilled projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dependence on reputation that heightens sensitivity to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: His 'indignation at literary wrongs' was ... a desire to ward off personal injuries ... this strengthens his argument against professional authorship, because literary wrongs would not have been injuries affecting his peace of mind, if he had not depended on his literary reputation ... for what ... was much more important than itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical warning: financial or psychological dependence on reputation makes writers more vulnerable to critics and parties; maintaining some independence reduces harmful sensitivity and reactive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile tradition with advancing thought
rubrics_metrics.description: The divinity of Scripture is a truth which no intellectual error can throw into total darkness ... men obscure and dishonor it by persisting in presenting it under the form which it seemed to wear in the twilight of reflection, even while a stronger day is revealing its true lineaments more clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or composing work that touches tradition or doctrine, allow for development of understanding; preserve core truths while permitting reformulation that better fits advancing thought; avoid clinging rigidly to twilight formulations that obscure the true lineaments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge merits regardless of national origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Much that is German may be found in the thoughts of our most marked writers ... When it is found to be Catholic, it is no longer admitted to be Teutonic, and unless it is hollow and visionary it is not recognised as German.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical fairness requires crediting ideas and merits regardless of their provenance; do not dismiss contributions because of national prejudice, nor refuse to identify influences because they become assimilated.
